what_its_for: Triamcinolone acetonide is a steroid medicine that reduces swelling, redness, and irritation in your body. It is used to treat many conditions including allergies, asthma, skin problems like eczema and psoriasis, joint pain and swelling (like arthritis), nasal allergies, and certain eye and mouth conditions. Your doctor may also use it as an injection to treat inflammation in a specific area of your body.
how_to_take: This medicine comes in several forms, and how you use it depends on what your doctor prescribed. For a nasal spray, gently blow your nose first, then spray into each nostril while breathing in slowly. For a skin cream or ointment, apply a thin layer to the affected area and gently rub it in. Do not cover the area with a bandage unless your doctor tells you to. For a mouth paste, dab a small amount onto the sore spot in your mouth at bedtime or as directed. If you receive an injection, it will be given by a healthcare provider in a clinic or office. Never inject this medicine yourself at home. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your form of this medication.
dosing: Your dose will depend on your condition, your age, your weight, and the form of triamcinolone you are using. Use exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not use more than directed, and do not use it more often or for longer than your doctor recommends. For nasal spray, adults and children over 2 years old typically use 1 to 2 sprays in each nostril once daily. For skin cream or ointment, apply a thin layer to the affected skin 2 to 4 times per day or as directed. Your doctor will give you specific dosing instructions that are right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take or use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra medicine to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not freeze this medicine. Keep the nasal spray bottle upright and replace the cap after each use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do not use more of this medicine than your doctor prescribed, and do not use it for longer than directed, as long-term or overuse of steroids can cause serious side effects. Avoid getting the nasal spray or cream in your eyes or mouth unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not apply skin cream to open wounds, infected skin, or your face unless specifically instructed. Try to avoid being around people who have chickenpox, measles, or other contagious illnesses while using this medicine, as steroids can weaken your immune system and make it easier to get sick. Do not stop using this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you have been using it for a long time. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it may increase the risk of stomach problems. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some drugs can interact with triamcinolone.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing; unusual weight gain or swelling; vision changes or eye pain; nosebleeds that do not stop or nasal sores; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or wounds that will not heal; muscle weakness or extreme tiredness; mood changes, depression, or unusual thoughts; increased thirst or urination which could be signs of high blood sugar; thinning or changes in your skin; or if your condition does not improve or gets worse after using this medicine as directed. Seek emergency help if you have a severe reaction.
when_it_works: How quickly this medicine works depends on how you are using it and what you are treating. For nasal allergy symptoms, you may start to notice improvement within 1 to 2 days, but it may take up to 1 to 2 weeks to feel the full benefit. For skin conditions, you may see improvement within a few days of use. For injections, relief from joint pain or inflammation often begins within a few days and can last several weeks to months. If you do not notice any improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use in children should be carefully supervised by a doctor. Long-term use of steroid medicines in children may slow growth. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time possible. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to the side effects of steroids, including bone thinning (osteoporosis), high blood sugar, and skin thinning. Talk to your doctor about any concerns. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Steroid medicines should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed and prescribed by your doctor. Breastfeeding: It is not fully known if triamcinolone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how your body handles this medication.
